objective: Compare the quality of a 16D dictionary with fuzzy grouped K=4D selection against the matched dense GELU baseline over three paired seeds.
hypothesis: One fixed-group winner out of every four stored features retains enough of the useful overcomplete-dictionary behavior to match or improve on dense validation loss at the parent sparse study's equal-algorithmic-FLOP endpoint.

budget.basis: equal algorithmic matrix FLOPs inherited from the exact sparse-autoencoder grid
budget.note: The fuzzy executed count bills redundant regular MXU contractions used to eliminate the exact gather/TopK bottleneck; it is reported as systems overhead, not used to shorten the learning horizon.

fuzzy_h16d_k4d.selector: one ReLU winner from each fixed exchangeable feature group
fuzzy_h16d_k4d.decoder: feature-specific row for every stored feature

stopping_rule: Run every fuzzy seed through its complete 2316-step cosine schedule; do not stop or retry based on intermediate loss.
